messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector switch to 'latency_first' on canary-03 we saw ~18% GPU memory growth and one OOM on the 4GPU pod. Not just latency changes, memory curve climbed steadily as batch sizes grew.

maya: raw excerpt from the canary log:```
[2026-03-15 02:11:08] replica=canary-03 memory.used_mb=8761 memory.free_mb=1743 batch.sz=6 avg_seq=512 pad_waste_pct=41.7 kv_cache_entries=12
[2026-03-15 02:11:37] replica=canary-03 memory.used_mb=10524 memory.free_mb=380 batch.sz=9 avg_seq=574 pad_waste_pct=44.1 kv_cache_entries=15
[2026-03-15 02:11:58] replica=canary-03 ERROR cuda\u003a out of memory when allocating 256 MB
```

alex: Yikes. Does the profiler show which kernel or allocation site grew?

maya: Short profiler snippet from runtime_profile (mem,top):```
kernel_select\u003alabel=softmax_fused workspace_mb=120 per_token_mb=0.23 calls=124
kernel_select\u003alabel=fused_gemm workspace_mb=460 per_token_mb=0.83 calls=78
batching\u003abehavior=batch_growth_rate=1.45 pad_overhead_mb=2.3 per_seq_meta_mb=0.14
kv_cache\u003aentries=15 avg_kv_bytes=245k spill=false
```

maya: Notice fused_gemm workspace_mb jumped after the selector change — probably the new kernel variant needs a larger workspace per batch. Also batch growth rate is high: we go from 6->9 quickly which multiplies workspace needs.

chris: I saw similar in yesterday's trace. The new fused_gemm variant allocates a tiled workspace for micro-batching and doesn't reuse intermediate buffers across requests.

alex: Quick mitigation options: 1) throttle batch growth (cap growth_rate to 1.15), 2) lower fused_gemm workspace via kernel param (tile_k=32 -> 16), 3) force fallback to the older gemm kernel when per-batch workspace > X MB.

maya: Patch idea (pseudo):```diff
- select_kernel(..., policy=latency_first)
+ select_kernel(..., policy=latency_first, max_workspace_mb=300, fallback_policy=cost_aware)
```

maya: Also I'm worried about KV cache interplay — when entries climb we stop reusing short-lived buffers because of LRU churn. We should reclaim transient buffers when kv_cache_entries > 10.

chris: Allocator knobs I'd try immediately: set REDWOOD_ALLOC_WORKSPACE_MB=1024 and REDWOOD_ALLOC_RECLAIM_AGE_SEC=5. That forces a shrink threshold and aggressive reclamation of inactive regions.

alex: Another low-risk change: dynamically group sequences into micro-batches by length percentile before continuous-batching aggregation. e.g., do batching within 0-25th, 25-50th, etc, to reduce pad waste. Should cut pad_waste_pct from ~44% to ~20-25% for current distribution.

maya: For the OOM stack:```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "runtime/inference_server.cc", line 942, in allocate_workspace
    gpu_mem_alloc(ptr, size) 
  File "/usr/lib/libcuda.so", line 128, in cudaMalloc
cuda\u003a out of memory
```

maya: I'm going to spin an experiment: revert kernel-selector to previous stable for 1h, apply allocator reclaim vars, and enable micro-grouping. Will run with RUNTIME_PROFILE=mem,latency for 2h.

infra-bot: Deployment started: revert/kernel-selector@release-2026-03-15 to canary-03 (sha: a1b2c3). Rolling restart on 4 pods.

alex: After revert, also please collect: per-request workspace footprint, per-token mem growth (delta) and per-seq meta bytes. If we can confirm per_token_mb for fused_gemm is really 0.83 then it's definitely the dominant driver.

chris: Long-term we should: 1) add buffer-reuse registry keyed by kernel_variant + workspace_shape, 2) implement passive buffer recycling after idle window, 3) update kernel selector cost model to include workspace_mb * cost_per_mb.

maya: Agreed. For the canary I added a lightweight buffer-reuse hack: if a buffer has same shape and last_used < now-2s reuse it. We'll see if it stabilizes without hurting latency.

alex: I'll run the micro-batching grouping sim overnight and post the sim stats here. If pad drop > 15% we keep it.

maya: Thanks — keeping watch. Will update with post-revert profile within 30m. :eyes:
